newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end up but off highs.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed up but off the day's highs on Monday due to locally-led profit- taking in selected secondaries in late trade, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 5.37 points, or 0.98 percent, to close at 554.40 points after reaching 556.08 in morning trade. Gainers led losers by 64 to 42, with 49 issues unchanged.

"If the Dow continues to gain tonight on perceptions that U.S. interest rates will be unchanged, it could boost market sentiment on Tuesday in Jakarta, but volume will be very limited," said an analyst from PT Nikko Securities Indonesia.

He compared the gains in Jakarta today with rallies in other Asian market. "It was a little bit exciting today but not as strong as other bourses in Asia as many foreign institutional operators have not regained confidence in Jakarta," he said.
"Market sentiment remains volatile and I don't expect any rally...unless there is real positive news from the Indonesia side," said a broker from a London-based brokerage firm.

Tyre-producer Gajah Tunggal fell 25 rupiah to 1,150 on volume of 6.4 million shares on local profit-taking after early gains. It was actively traded on speculative interest following the August announcement of a forthcoming rights issues.
Blue-chips telecommunications firm Telkom, satellite firm Indosat and cigarette makers Gudang Garam and Sampoerna were among the targets for foreign buying.

Heavyweight Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 3,350 on a turnover of 2.6 million shares. Brokers said the rise was also due to a report that the firm expected revenue growth of 15-25 percent in 1996 and that it had no plan to float additional shares.
Pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma and its subsidiary Igar Jaya were actively traded on reports that Kalba planned to announce a stock split and reduce its stake in Igar Jaya, brokers said.
Glass and plastics producer for pharmaceutical products, Igar Jaya, rose 200 rupiah to 2,775 on volume of 3.5 million shares.
Kalbe Farma rose 400 rupiah to 5,525 on a volume of 2.3 million shares. Brokers said the rise was also due to "buy" recommendation from some analysts on its 1996 and 1997 net profit prospects.
